goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 — Mobile light-theme `.user-card .name` changes primary lightness from 30% to 50%, causing the same emphasis regression.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in mobile/user.scss line 497, the `.name` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light-theme lightness from 30% to 50%, making the text lighter/less emphasized. This is inconsistent with other similar changes in the diff (e.g., desktop/user.scss line 119-122 maintains 30% for light theme in the `.username a` and `.name` selectors). This appears to be an unintentional regression in text emphasis for the mobile light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — Mobile light-theme `.custom-message-length` changes primary lightness from 70% to 30%, inverting hint styling relative to the desktop rule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This means for light themes, the lightness changed from 70% to 30%, which is a significant inversion. In contrast, the desktop version at desktop/modal.scss line 91 uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, maintaining 70% lightness for light themes. This inconsistency between mobile and desktop for the same `.custom-message-length` class appears to be a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — Linked-topic card `h3` light-theme branch changes primary lightness from 20% to 50%, losing stronger title contrast.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a change in mobile/topic-post.scss at line 182. The diff shows the h3 color changing from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch (first argument to dark-light-choose) uses 50% lightness instead of the original 20%, which would indeed result in a lighter, less contrasted title color in light themes. This appears to be an inconsistency compared to other similar changes in the codebase where the light-theme branch typically preserves the original lightness value.
